thingsToDo.title: Clematis Street and the waterfront
thingsToDo.description: Walk downtown from Clematis Street to the lagoon for restaurants, public spaces, events, and skyline views.

thingsToDo.title: Norton Museum of Art
thingsToDo.description: Use the major art museum as an indoor anchor during hot or rainy periods and pair it with nearby downtown neighborhoods.

thingsToDo.title: Mounts Botanical Garden
thingsToDo.description: Explore tropical and subtropical plants at Palm Beach County's botanical garden near the airport.

thingsToDo.title: Grassy Waters Preserve
thingsToDo.description: See part of the freshwater wetland system west of the city through boardwalks, trails, and guided nature programs.

thingsToDo.title: Antique Row and historic neighborhoods
thingsToDo.description: Explore South Dixie Highway and nearby residential districts for design, shops, and a more local urban experience.

thingsToDo.title: Palm Beach — separate town
thingsToDo.description: Cross the lagoon for Worth Avenue, beaches, and historic architecture, while keeping Palm Beach distinct from West Palm Beach.

bestTimeToVisit.title: Cooler months are easiest for outdoor planning
bullets: Late fall through early spring generally brings lower humidity and comfortable outdoor conditions.
Summer is hot, humid, and storm-prone; start exposed activities early and keep afternoon plans flexible.
Busy winter and holiday periods reward advance reservations for popular tours and timed attractions.

travelTips: Group each day by geography instead of crossing the region repeatedly.
Use early mornings for exposed outdoor activities and waterfront time.
Check park, marine, and weather conditions before nature-focused plans.
Treat nearby municipalities and protected areas as separate destinations with their own access rules.

faq.q: How many days should I plan for West Palm Beach?
faq.a: Two to three days is a good starting point for the core sights plus one outdoor or regional experience.

faq.q: Is West Palm Beach good for outdoor travelers?
faq.a: Yes. The strongest itineraries combine the destination itself with nearby water, parks, preserves, or trails.
It depends on the destination, but a car or guided tour is often useful for protected lands and regional excursions.

faq.q: Should I book tours in advance?
faq.a: For high-demand wildlife, boating, park, and holiday-period experiences, advance booking is sensible.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: West Palm Beach is an incorporated mainland city on the western shore of the Lake Worth Lagoon.

sections.heading: Geography & setting
paragraphs: Across the lagoon lies the separate Town of Palm Beach on a barrier island, while freshwater wetlands extend inland to the west.

sections.heading: History & culture
paragraphs: Downtown redevelopment, historic neighborhoods, arts institutions, and proximity to Palm Beach shape the city's modern identity.

sections.heading: Outdoor & seasonal highlights
paragraphs: Waterfront walking, wetlands, botanical gardens, and regional beaches provide the outdoor balance.

sections.heading: Getting around
paragraphs: Downtown is compact, but a car or rideshare helps with Grassy Waters, gardens, and cross-lagoon trips.
